firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
The Paper Track submission requirements say that optional notebooks, project links, and attached Kaggle Resources must be public (or become public after the deadline). The Competition Data Security rule says not to publish or make Competition Data available to people who have not formally agreed to the rules.

Our paper's verification archive includes raw agent traces, command transcripts, patches, supplied harness wheels, and small source/test fragments from the Gemma 4 Developer Agent Competition. We will not publish that archive through an unrestricted link.

Is there an approved restricted channel through which Paper Track judges may verify such an archive, with access limited to people covered by the relevant competition rules? If not, should the public companion contain only aggregate results, manifests, author-owned code, and synthetic controls, while the raw archive remains retained but unavailable publicly?
